Thus, the visiting of the schools being completed, we have only briefly to report concerning the state of the congregation of this place, that one has in the same 134 Dutch communicants and approximately 24 Sinhalese communicants. But how most of them acquit themselves of their duty, and how little work is done among high and low, young and old, regarding public worship, is so well known that we deem it unnecessary to mention anything of it. The number of those baptized in this congregation is from the end of August 1750 to the end of August 1751, 31 children, both boys and girls, and on Mature [uncertain: possibly a location or administrative division] 9 children, together 40 children. The number of those married in this congregation is from the end of August 1750 to the end of August 1751, 9 pairs, and on Mature 2 pairs, together 11 pairs. The number of those deceased in this congregation is from the end of August 1750 to the end of August 1751, 28 persons, and that on Mature 8, together 36 persons. That is then, Esteemed Sir, what we have to report concerning the church and school visitation of this Command, when we now compare this our finding with the reports of some preceding years, we shall perceive that the number of schoolchildren is considerably diminishing, thus the Sinhalese Christendom's knowledge going more backward than forward.

--- CHUNK 3 ---
The principal reason for this is that the monetary penalties, which previously were imposed on those who neglected church and school attendance, as well as on those living in a state of concubinage, have now been abolished. This has had the effect among the careless people that they have since that time concerned themselves little or not at all with church and school attendance. One gives this into consideration whether it would not be better if those penalties were reintroduced on the former footing. It is true that true Christianity does not wish to be propagated by force or by compulsion, but it is on the other hand also true that a Sinhalese, almost in no matter, can be moved to fulfill his duty without threat and without compulsion. We do not regard the monetary penalties as a means of force to compel them to convert to Christianity, but only as a means that should give the Sinhalese occasion to fulfill his duty regarding Christianity, which serves for the salvation of their souls. And we also cannot regard the Sinhalese, although aged, as those who have come to the full use of their understanding, but as children who must continually be kept under the rod of discipline due to lack of understanding. And indeed among the Sinhalese, when we compare them with our cultivated European people, we find but little reasonable action in the soul.

--- CHUNK 4 ---
We give this into consideration of our Illustrious superiors, and we shall await their good judgment thereupon with patience. Meanwhile we further wish that God Almighty would pour out richly upon our Illustrious superiors the spirit of wisdom, of knowledge, of counsel, and of understanding. May He bless all their counsels, and in particular those which might be taken for the support of that so very declining Christendom. May He make their government all-seeing, so that they may show themselves not only as examples of true godliness, but also as leaders of the Lord's church, through whose efforts the kingdom of Jesus may be extended. But in particular, Your Esteemed Sir, may God Almighty take you into His gracious protection, fill you with His spirit, endow you with all necessary spiritual and bodily strength, and make you faithful in that post in which His Divine providence has placed you, so that justice and righteousness may be maintained in the land, and we under our vine and fig tree may enjoy the good of the land. This we wish with heart and soul, understanding Your Esteemed and well-commanding Sir! Your Esteemed very humble and obedient servants, signed A. F. Schultze and C. van Dam.
